title: Protocol for Isolation of Cardiac Interstitial Cells from Adult Murine Hearts for Unbiased Single Cell Profiling
protocol: Euthanize the mouse according to the protocol approved by your Institution.
Place the euthanized mouse on the dissection stage in supine position.
Fix the paws of the mouse in place with four needles/pins.
Dissociate adult murine cardiac ventricular tissue to isolate single interstitial cells.
Spray with 70% ethanol.
Cut the skin below the thoracic cavity.
Pull the skin up and place it under two top needles/pins.
Use a different set of tools for internal organs to avoid mycoplasma contamination from fur/skin.
Hold the lower edge of the sternum and pull it slightly upward.
Cut upward along the right side of the sternum.
Cut down on the diaphragm from the right side to the left side of the mouse.
Cut up on the left side to expose the full cavity.
Run tools along the abdominal aorta upward and cut the heart from the back.
Collect the heart still beating in a dish containing HBSS.
Dissect out the atria and outflow tract.
Place the dissected parts on ice.
Inject mice intraperitoneally with Heparin, 5 min before culling, at a dose of 50 USP units per mouse.
Cut the myocardium into small pieces, approximately 1 mm in size, using a blade or scalpel on a bacteriological petri dish.
Add 1 mL of enzymatic solution to the myocardial pieces and mince again to obtain homogeneous-sized pieces.
Transfer the tissue suspension into an autoclaved Erlenmeyer flask (50 mL) with a magnetic bar, adding additional 7 mL of enzymatic solution.
Use a wide bore 1 mL transfer pipette to complete the transfer.
Aspirate some enzymatic solution before collecting tissue fragments to avoid unwanted adhesion to the dry plastic surface of tip/pipette.
Place the flask in glass troughs filled with distilled water pre-warmed at 37°C on a magnetic stirrer.
Agitate the flask at 250 rpm for the first 15 min digestion at 37°C.
Gently pipette the suspension and collect the supernatant in a pre-assembled collection tube on ice (50 mL tube topped with a 40 μm cell strainer, pre-wet with 1 mL of FBS).
Add 7 mL of enzymatic solution to the remaining tissue fragments for a second 15 min digestion at 37°C.
Wash the cell strainer with 3 mL of wash buffer (2% FCS in PBS) after the second digestion.
Collect the cell suspension through the strainer and wash it with 3 mL of wash buffer.
Pre-warn 1 mL aliquots of RBC lysis buffer at 37°C, in 1.5 mL tubes (one per each sample).
Spin down the cell suspension preferably in a refrigerated centrifuge for 30 s at 600 × g and then for 5 min at 300 × g.
Resuspend cell pellets in 1 mL pre-warmed RBC lysis buffer.
Transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of wash buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Alternatively, perform RBC lysis directly in the original 50 mL collection tube.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 minute.
Dilute with 10 mL of wash buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from the cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL dead cell removal beads.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 20°C–22°C in the dark.
Transfer the bead-cell suspension into a 15 mL tube with 6 mL of binding buffer.
Place the tube under the uptake port of the AutoMACS instrument.
Select the “Separation” menu and then choose the depletion program “DepleteS” from the touchscreen.
After completion, start the “QRinse” cleaning program before proceeding to the next sample.
Centrifuge the eluted cell suspension in two 5 mL FACS tubes.
Resuspend each pellet in 500 μL of FACS buffer with DRAQ5.
Divide the cell suspension into two flow cytometry round bottom 5 mL tubes.
Spin for 8 minutes at 400 × g.
Resuspend the cell pellets in FACS buffer (500 μL per tube).
Add DRAQ5 to a final concentration of 2 μM and incubate for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Add Propidium iodine to a final concentration of 3 μM.
Transfer the cells onto ice.
Prepare collection tubes with 50-100 μL of collection buffer.
Vortex or place on a tube roller shaker to equilibrate the tube walls with the buffer.
Use a flow cytometer at a temperature of 4°C with a 130 μm nozzle.
Collect between 24,000 and 32,000 events per sample.
Maintain the flow rate between 900 and 1,100 events per second.
Ensure sorting efficiency is over 90%.
Collect samples for approximately 2 minutes to obtain the desired number of events.
Sort the minimum number of events required for loading the right number of cells in the 10× Chromium chip.
Transfer the collection tubes with sorted cells on ice.
Add 800 μL of collection buffer per tube.
Centrifuge at 300g for 8 minutes in a refrigerated swing bucket microcentrifuge.
Spin for 4 minutes, then turn the tubes and spin for an additional 4 minutes if using a fixed rotor centrifuge.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving approximately 40 μL of collection buffer.
Proceed with the 10× Chromium protocol.
Use fresh 80% ethanol for all purification steps.
